data.reasoning: The package is a standard KDE application. The PKGBUILD downloads the source tarball and its PGP signature from the official KDE download server. The SHA256 checksum for the signature is set to SKIP, which is standard Arch packaging practice since the signature is verified via validpgpkeys. There are no malicious injections, no unexpected network requests, and no suspicious build instructions. The disagreement is solely due to an API error in the Qwen model during the full review phase.
data.disagreement_analysis: The Qwen model returned 'inconclusive' because it encountered an HTTP 400 API error when reviewing the PKGBUILD during the full file review phase, despite successfully passing the initial PKGBUILD parse. The Deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and correctly identified the package as safe.
coverage_issues: Qwen model failed to complete the PKGBUILD review due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400).
learnings: When an LLM API request fails during the full file review phase, the tool should fall back to the initial PKGBUILD parse result if it was successful, rather than marking the entire package as inconclusive.
Implement retry logic for transient LLM API errors before failing the audit or marking the result as inconclusive.
